observations: A flat orange border frames a densely layered face-like form; two mismatched eye shapes—one square-ish on the left, one rectangular on the right—sit at different heights, each outlined in yellow and black with white highlights inside.
A wide open mouth near the lower center shows vertical white stripes between orange-outlined lips, while a triangular nose shape points downward between the eyes.
Overlapping scribble lines in white, teal, pink, green, and black radiate outward from the face across the entire field, thickening into a spiky mass around the edges.
reading: The face pushes close to the picture edge, leaving almost no open ground. Its two eye forms refuse to match—one sits higher, one lower—and the striped mouth hangs open in a way that reads as alarm or raw noise. The scribble field around it is not background decoration; it presses inward, competing with the face for attention. The flat orange border holds all of this just barely in place.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nifty faces #126 and nnxyz nifty faces #128. Title order and recorded creation order align here, though neither confirms a making sequence across the full catalogue.

connections.reason: Both works center a wide-open toothed mouth, but #126 uses a dark volumetric mask form against a warm striped field, while #127 dissolves its face into surrounding scribble on a flat orange ground—a direct contrast in how edge and interior are handled.

Both images use paired rectangular eye shapes at slightly different heights and a horizontal tooth-row mouth, but nnotb #145 spreads its marks across a teal field with open surrounding space, whereas #127 packs the scribble mass tightly against the face with no open ground.

lookingQuestion: The two eye shapes sit at different heights and have different outlines—what does that asymmetry do to the way you read the face as a whole?
ambiguities: The spiky mass surrounding the face could be read as hair, fur, or purely abstract mark-making; no supplied evidence resolves which reading is supported.

The nnotb #145 comparison is from a different owned series; the formal parallel in eye and mouth structure is visible in both inspected images, but the connection across series reflects the collector's observed pattern, not a stated relationship.
